versions.shortDescription: CSV-to-CSV one-hot encoding using pandas only.
versions.longDescription:
# OneHotEncoding

OneHotEncoding is a lightweight CSV → CSV preprocessing tool that performs pandas-only one-hot encoding on categorical columns, producing a tabular output suitable for downstream ML workflows.

It is designed to be simple, dependency-minimal (just pandas), and configurable for common encoding variants (drop-first, NaN dummies, custom prefix separator, etc.).

## What this tool does
- Reads an input CSV table (features) and produces an encoded CSV (encoded) with the same number of rows and additional dummy columns.
- Preserves an optional identifier column
- If the first column is named id (case-insensitive), it is treated as an identifier and kept as the first column in the output.
- All other columns are treated as feature columns.
- Selects which columns to encode
- If columns is provided (comma-separated list), only those columns are encoded.
- If columns is empty, the tool automatically selects:
- all object and category dtype columns
- boolean columns only if bool_to_number = false (otherwise booleans are handled separately)
- Generates dummy variables using pandas.get_dummies
- Adds one dummy column per category value per encoded feature (or k-1 if drop_first=true).
- Dummy column naming is controlled by prefix_sep (default: __), e.g. color__red.
- Optional behaviors
- drop_first: drop the first category per feature (reduces multicollinearity by producing k-1 dummies).
- dummy_na: create a dedicated dummy column for missing values (NaN) in encoded columns.
- keep_original: keep original categorical columns alongside the generated dummies (otherwise they are replaced by dummies).
- Emits basic metrics
- n_rows, n_cols, and n_encoded_input_cols are sent as metrics after encoding.

## Configuration

Hyperparameters
- columns (STRING, default: "")
Comma-separated list of columns to one-hot encode.
If empty: auto-detect categorical columns (object/category; plus bool if bool_to_number=false).
- drop_first (BOOLEAN, default: 0)
If true, drop the first category per encoded feature (k-1 dummies).
- bool_to_number (BOOLEAN, default: 1)
If true, boolean columns are converted to numeric 0/1 instead of being one-hot encoded.
- dummy_na (BOOLEAN, default: 0)
If true, include a dummy column for missing values in encoded columns.
- handle_unknown (CATEGORICAL, default: ignore)
Present for API consistency. Note: pandas.get_dummies encodes categories observed in the input; it does not implement a “future unknown category” handling mode like some sklearn encoders.
- prefix_sep (STRING, default: "__")
Separator between the source column name and category in dummy column names (e.g., city__Berlin).
- keep_original (BOOLEAN, default: 0)
If true, original categorical columns are retained in addition to the dummy columns.

## Inputs
- features (CSV, required)
Input table. May contain numeric and categorical columns.
If the first column is named id, it is preserved as an identifier column.

## Outputs
- encoded (CSV)
One-hot encoded table with the same rows and additional dummy columns.

hyperparams.description: If true, drop the first category per feature (k-1 dummies).

hyperparams.description: If true, keep original categorical columns in addition to dummy columns.

hyperparams.description: If true, convert boolean columns to numeric 0/1 instead of one-hot encoding them.

hyperparams.name: columns
hyperparams.description: Comma-separated list of columns to one-hot encode. If empty, all object/category/bool columns are encoded.

hyperparams.name: dummy_na
hyperparams.description: If true, create a dedicated dummy column for NaN values in encoded columns.

hyperparams.name: handle_unknown
hyperparams.description: How to handle unknown categories. Kept for consistency; pandas.get_dummies encodes categories present in the input.

hyperparams.description: Separator between column name and category in generated dummy column names.
